requirements.text: The EIRENE System Requirements Specification defines a radio system satisfying the mobile communications requirements of the European railways [EIRENE FRS].
Compliance to the list of normative documents is mandatory for all of the GSM services necessary to provide the functionality specified in the [EIRENE FRS].

The following minimum values shall apply: coverage probability of 95% based on a coverage level of 38.5 dBµV/m (-98 dBm) for voice and non-safety critical data; coverage probability of 95% based on a coverage level of 41.5 dBµV/m (-95 dBm) on lines with ETCS levels 2/3 for speeds lower than or equal to 220km/h.
The EIRENE mobile installation shall be designed to operate in a network meeting the criteria in 3.2.2 and 3.2.3.
Call setup times as defined in the EIRENE FRS shall be achieved with authentication and ciphering procedures enabled.
The network shall operate in a sub-band, or combination of sub-bands, of the R-GSM band as defined in [EN 301 515, Index [35]].
The network shall terminate the ongoing VGCS/VBS call if it receives the 3-digit sequence “***” transmitted via DTMF signals.

In order to minimise the discomfort caused by the DTMF tone added in the voice channel, the duration of the tone generated by the fixed line dispatcher shall be 70ms ± 5ms, and there shall be a minimum gap of 65ms between each tone.
The muting and unmuting for VGCS shall be in line with [EN 301 515, Index [4]].
All SIM cards used in EIRENE mobiles shall comply with the requirements of the MORANE FFFIS for GSM-R SIM Cards [MORANE SIM].
All mobiles shall be capable of operation in the following frequency bands: Railway GSM (R-GSM) 876-915/921-960.
Mobile radios shall be of the following power classes: Cab radio 2 (8W), General purpose radio 4* (2W*), Operational radio 4* (2W*).

If a Railway emergency call set up from an EIRENE radio is unsuccessful, the radio shall automatically re-attempt the call setup until the call setup is successful, a retry timer expires (duration 30 seconds, as specified in the [EIRENE FRS]) or the user abandons the call.
A service availability indication shall be provided to radio users, as defined in [EN 301 515, Index [26]].
The user shall be prevented from entering direct mode if the GSM service is available.
If the attempt to establish a Railway emergency call is not successful after 2 seconds, an indication shall be provided to the user of the status of the establishment request procedure.

All EIRENE mobile equipment shall comply with all environmental, EMC and physical specifications defined in the GSM standard, especially with reference to [GSM 05.90 and EN 301 515, Index [2] & [35]].
All EIRENE mobile equipment shall conform to [EN 60950] (Safety of Information Technology Equipment), including Electrical Business Equipment, 1993, plus amendments A1 and A2.
EIRENE mobile equipment shall be capable of operating over a standard range of temperatures from -20°C to +55°C.
EIRENE mobile equipment shall be capable of being stored (ie without being operational) at temperatures down to -40°C without any permanent damage.
The equipment shall be capable of coping with temperature variations of up to +/- 1°C/minute.
EIRENE mobile equipment shall be capable of operating between altitudes of -100m and 1800m, referenced to sea level.
The equipment shall be able to cope with relative humidities of 100% for short periods, although the yearly average is expected to be 75%.
The equipment shall also cope with 95% humidity for 30 days in the year.
Operationally caused infrequent and slight moisture condensation shall not lead to any malfunction or failure.
All equipment shall not degrade photochemically when exposed to solar radiation of up to 1200 W/m2.
All EIRENE mobile equipment shall be protected against shock and vibration in compliance with standards defined in [prEN 50125] using tests defined in [prEN 50155].
All handheld mobile equipment shall be capable of withstanding the following shocks: non-repetitive shocks of up to 3g for up to 100ms under normal conditions; free fall from 0.5m.
EIRENE mobile equipment shall be capable of being subjected to both sinusoidal and random vibration.
Handheld mobile equipment shall be capable of withstanding the following levels of continuous sinusoidal vibration: frequency range: 5-200 Hz; peak-to-peak amplitude: 7.5 mm; peak acceleration: 1.5g.
The random vibrations to be withstood by mobile equipment shall be 0.25g in all three axes of freedom.
Battery requirements shall be provided without the use of discontinuous reception or transmission (DTX/DRX).
Battery requirements shall be met based on full power during transmission and assuming hourly periodic location updating.
All EIRENE mobile equipment shall be immune to external EMC as defined in [ENV 50121 part 4].

The transmission of EM radiation from all EIRENE mobile equipment shall comply with the radio frequency transmission masks defined in [EN 301 515, Index [35]] for the range of GSM frequencies defined in section 1 of this document.
Where the emission levels defined by [EN 301 515, Index [35]] exceed those stated in [ENV 50121 part 4], the GSM specification shall take precedence.
Mobile equipment shall comply with the generic standard for EMC in the industrial environment as defined in [ENV 50081 part 2], except for emissions at GSM frequencies as noted above.
The environmental and physical tolerance of the EIRENE mobile radio units shall be tested at a facility in accordance with [EN 45001].
All EMC emission and immunity tests shall be performed in accordance with guidelines defined in the [EN 61000-4] series and in [EN 50140].
Environmental testing procedures shall follow guidelines defined in [IEC 68 part 1].

Specific environmental test procedures to be followed for EIRENE mobile equipment shall include the following tests as defined in the [IEC 68] series: A Cold; B Dry heat; D Damp heat (cyclic); E Impact; F Vibration; G Acceleration; K Corrosive atmospheres; M Air pressure; N Change of temperature; P Fire hazard.
Upon an appropriate MMI action, the radio shall initiate a call to the appropriate controller with ‘Railway operation’ priority (see section 10.2).
The calling driver’s functional number shall be passed to the network using UUS1.
On receipt of a ‘Call other drivers in area’ request, the radio shall initiate a group call using the ‘all trains’ group identification (see section 9) with eMLPP priority level 2 (see section 10.2).
Activation of the ‘Railway emergency call’ function shall cause the radio to initiate a Railway emergency call as defined in section 13.
Where there is more than one active cab, the radio connection shall be provided using the GSM Multi-Party service.
The multi-party call shall have ‘Railway operation’ priority (see section 10.2) and whilst on-going a ‘multi-drivers’ indication shall be displayed permanently at all Cab radios.
Upon activation of the function ‘Call train staff’, the radio shall determine the appropriate functional number based on the staff member selected and the train number (see section 9).
A GSM point-to-point voice call at ‘Railway operation’ priority (see section 10.2) shall then be initiated.
The Cab radio shall be capable of being used as a standard GSM telephone, such that the driver is able to call any valid number subject to closed user group, call barring or other restrictions.
The Cab radio shall be able to receive, display and store incoming short (SMS) text messages (see section 12).
The Cab radio shall support shunting mode communications as defined in section 14.
When switched on, the radio shall initiate automatic self-testing using the GSM IMSI attach procedure (including the automatic selection of the default loudspeaker volume – see table 5-1).
Upon switch on, the Cab radio shall be registered with a mobile network (see section 10.5).
If registration is not successful an audible and visual indication shall be provided.
Upon registration, the mobile shall be accessible by calling the MSISDN or the Engine or Coach number with which it is associated.
This shall require the home network database to maintain this correlation.
Upon activation of the registration function, a USSD message (see section 11) shall be sent by the Cab radio.
Upon activation of the deregistration function, a USSD message (see section 11) shall be sent by the Cab radio.

Upon detection (automatically or based on a list stored in the Cab radio) of the additional on-train functions for equipment physically connected to the Cab radio, a USSD message (see section 11) shall be sent by the Cab radio after activation of the registration or deregistration function.
This procedure shall take place at the installation of the Cab radio.
On-train functions for equipment physically connected to the Cab radio shall be registered or deregistered automatically based on a USSD message (see section 11) sent by the Cab radio.
The system shall implement A5/3 (KASUMI) or higher for air interface encryption and use MILENAGE for authentication to ensure robust security.
The Cab radio shall implement a strict security policy that disables non-essential GSM services (e.g., public internet access, non-railway SMS) to minimize the attack surface.
Define the specific retry interval (e.g., exponential backoff or fixed 2-second intervals) to ensure predictable behavior during network congestion.
Specify the mandatory components to be tested (e.g., antenna, SIM, transceiver) and the required behavior if a test fails (e.g., enter safe mode, alert driver).
Define a mandatory maximum handover interruption time (e.g., 'The handover interruption time shall not exceed 300ms') to ensure service continuity for safety-critical communications.
Explicitly state the maximum allowable call setup latency (e.g., < 2 seconds) for high-priority emergency calls to ensure timely response.

OPEN: The PRD mentions the use of USSD for registration and functional numbering but does not define the security controls for these messages, potentially exposing them to interception or spoofing. - All USSD messages used for functional registration and location-dependent addressing shall be protected by the underlying GSM signaling security mechanisms (ciphering and integrity protection).

OPEN: The PRD requires the home network database to maintain correlation between MSISDN and Engine/Coach numbers but does not specify the required availability or synchronization latency for this database. - Define the maximum allowable synchronization latency and availability requirements (e.g., 99.999%) for the routing database to ensure reliable functional addressing.

OPEN: The PRD specifies network coverage and handover success rates but does not define the expected subscriber density or concurrent call volume per cell/area. - Specify the maximum number of concurrent voice group calls and individual sessions per cell to ensure the network infrastructure can handle peak operational loads.
